name: Student Assessment Trend Summary
description: Takes rows (array) and produces trend_summary (string) in 2 steps. Step 1: aggregates numeric columns in a result-row array into compact summary rows and returns the aggregate rows, takes rows (array) as input and outputs rows (array). Step 2: summarizes the trend in a student's result rows over recent attempts, such as improving, declining, or stable. Returns a plain-text trend description, takes assessment_rows (array) from step 1 as input and outputs trend_summary (string).

name: Grounded Multilingual SQL Results
description: Takes chunks (array), language_records (array), target_language (string), query (string), answer_summary (string) and sql (string) and produces result (array) in 4 steps. Step 1: filters text chunks down to those requiring translation by keeping chunks whose detected language differs from the target language code, takes chunks (array), language_records (array) and target_language (string) as input and outputs chunks_to_translate (array). Step 2: detects bibliographic citations in text chunks and returns citation records with surrounding context, takes text_chunks (array) from step 1 as input and outputs citation_records (array). Step 3: checks whether the answer summary is supported by the cited passages for the query, takes query (string), answer_summary (string) and citations (array) from step 2 as input and outputs supported (boolean). Step 4: executes an SQL query against the input dataset and returns the result rows, takes sql (string) and is_safe (boolean) from step 3 as input and outputs result (array).

name: Provenance-Checked Weather Summaries
description: Takes report (string), sql (string), variable_name (string), period_granularity (string) and summary_metric (string) and produces summary (array) in 4 steps. Step 1: checks whether a provenance report lists required sources and transformations and returns a compliance flag, takes report (string) as input and outputs flag (boolean). Step 2: executes an SQL query against the input dataset and returns the result rows, takes sql (string) and is_safe (boolean) from step 1 as input and outputs result (array). Step 3: converts generic result rows into normalized weather reading records for one measured variable, takes rows (array) from step 2 and variable_name (string) as input and outputs readings (array). Step 4: groups weather readings by time period and computes the chosen summary metric, takes readings (array) from step 3, period_granularity (string) and summary_metric (string) as input and outputs summary (array).

name: Compliant Weather SQL Readings Normalizer
description: Takes report (string), sql (string) and variable_name (string) and produces readings (array) in 3 steps. Step 1: checks whether a provenance report lists required sources and transformations and returns a compliance flag, takes report (string) as input and outputs flag (boolean). Step 2: executes an SQL query against the input dataset and returns the result rows, takes sql (string) and is_safe (boolean) from step 1 as input and outputs result (array). Step 3: converts generic result rows into normalized weather reading records for one measured variable, takes rows (array) from step 2 and variable_name (string) as input and outputs readings (array).

name: Weather SQL Period Summary
description: Takes sql (string), is_safe (boolean), variable_name (string), period_granularity (string) and summary_metric (string) and produces summary (array) in 3 steps. Step 1: executes an SQL query against the input dataset and returns the result rows, takes sql (string) and is_safe (boolean) as input and outputs result (array). Step 2: converts generic result rows into normalized weather reading records for one measured variable, takes rows (array) from step 1 and variable_name (string) as input and outputs readings (array). Step 3: groups weather readings by time period and computes the chosen summary metric, takes readings (array) from step 2, period_granularity (string) and summary_metric (string) as input and outputs summary (array).

name: Seasonal Time Series Change Points
description: Takes series (array), window_size (number), season_length (number) and threshold (number) and produces change_points (array) in 3 steps. Step 1: smooths a time series with a moving average window and returns the smoothed time series, takes series (array) and window_size (number) as input and outputs smoothed (array). Step 2: decomposes a time series into a trend component and a seasonal profile for a fixed seasonal period, takes series (array) from step 1 and season_length (number) as input and outputs trend (array) and seasonality (object). Step 3: detects abrupt level or trend changes in a time series using a sensitivity threshold, takes series (array) from step 2 and threshold (number) as input and outputs change_points (array).

name: Seasonal Change Point Detector
description: Takes series (array), season_length (number) and threshold (number) and produces change_points (array) in 2 steps. Step 1: decomposes a time series into a trend component and a seasonal profile for a fixed seasonal period, takes series (array) and season_length (number) as input and outputs trend (array) and seasonality (object). Step 2: detects abrupt level or trend changes in a time series using a sensitivity threshold, takes series (array) from step 1 and threshold (number) as input and outputs change_points (array).

name: Survey Job Answer Summary
description: Takes survey_response_records (array) and query (string) and produces answer_summary (string) in 2 steps. Step 1: extracts free-text job titles, employer names, and duty descriptions from survey response records into text chunks. Each chunk keeps a response identifier, takes survey_response_records (array) as input and outputs text_chunks (array). Step 2: generates an answer summary for a query from retrieved text chunks, takes query (string) and passages (array) from step 1 as input and outputs answer_summary (string).

name: Index Passage Summary Generator
description: Takes query (string) and index (object) and produces summary (string) in 2 steps. Step 1: retrieves text chunks from a search index using lexical BM25 scoring, takes query (string) and index (object) as input and outputs passages (array). Step 2: summarizes an array of text chunks into a shorter plain-text summary, takes chunks (array) from step 1 as input and outputs summary (string).

name: Weighted Survey Entity Enrichment
description: Takes weighted_survey_records (array), column_mapping (object) and entity_link_records (array) and produces enriched_entity_records (array) in 2 steps. Step 1: builds a cross-tabulation table from weighted survey records using the row and column variables named in the column mapping. It returns result rows with unweighted counts, weighted counts, and percentages, takes weighted_survey_records (array) and column_mapping (object) as input and outputs result_rows (array). Step 2: joins query result rows to entity link records to add graph-derived fields to each entity record. Returns enriched entity records without changing unrelated fields, takes entity_link_records (array) and result_rows (array) from step 1 as input and outputs enriched_entity_records (array).

name: Image Similarity Dataset Recommendation
description: Takes embeddings (array), query (string) and limit (number) and produces candidates (array) in 4 steps. Step 1: builds a nearest-neighbor retrieval index from image embeddings so that images can be compared by visual similarity, takes embeddings (array) as input and outputs index (object). Step 2: retrieves text chunks from a search index using dense vector similarity, takes query (string) and index (object) from step 1 as input and outputs passages (array). Step 3: extracts weighted key phrases from an array of text chunks and returns keyword records, takes chunks (array) from step 2 as input and outputs keywords (array). Step 4: searches a dataset retrieval index using keyword records and returns ranked dataset identifiers. It applies the recommendation limit to the candidate list, takes keywords (array) from step 3, index (object) from step 1 and limit (number) as input and outputs candidates (array).
